locations.rationale: Property assignment `name: this.baseUrl` in the object literal returned by ApiClient.fetchUser; the literal is contextually typed as User by the declared return type, so this token resolves to the User.name declaration.
Property access `user.name` in formatUser; `user` is the parameter typed User, so the access resolves to the User.name declaration.
Property access `user.name` in app.ts; `user` is explicitly annotated as User (imported from ./api), so the access resolves to the User.name declaration.
Exact-name token `name` in `const name = user.name;` is the identifier of a new local variable declaration; it resolves to that local binding, not to the User.name interface property.

records.rationale: The declaration is the `name` property of interface User (api.ts line 2). Exhaustive scan of the two-file fixture found four exact `name` identifier tokens outside the declaration range. Three semantically resolve to User.name: the contextually typed object-literal property in fetchUser's return (api.ts 13:17), the access `user.name` in formatUser (api.ts 18:14), and the access `user.name` in app.ts (app.ts 6:18). The local `const name` in app.ts (6:6) resolves to its own variable binding and is excluded. No import/export binding token for the property exists under the bindings_optional policy (the `type User` import binds the interface, not the property), so no optional binding locations are reported. definitionUsage is the first required location after sorting by URI, start line, then start character.
